title: passive: be and past participle
rule: The passive is a form of be plus the past participle. English is spoken here. Not English is spoke.
ruleRu: Пассив — форма be и третья форма глагола. English is spoken here.
exampleOk: The window was broken last night.
exampleBad: The window was broke last night.
l1Trap: Пассив строят без третьей формы: was break, is spoke.

title: by in the passive
rule: Use by only when the doer matters. Leave by out when the doer is unknown. My bike was stolen.
ruleRu: By — только если важно, кто сделал. Если исполнитель неизвестен, by не нужен.
exampleOk: The letter was sent yesterday.
exampleBad: The letter was sent by someone yesterday.
l1Trap: By someone добавляют всегда.

title: say and tell
rule: Tell needs a person right after it: tell me. Say does not: say that, say to me. Not She said me.
ruleRu: После tell сразу человек: tell me. Say человека не требует. Не She said me.
exampleOk: He told me he was busy. He said he was busy.
exampleBad: He said me he was busy.
l1Trap: Said me строится по русскому «сказал мне».

title: reported speech
rule: When the reporting verb is past, the tense usually steps back. Will becomes would. She said she was tired.
ruleRu: Если глагол сообщения в прошлом, время обычно сдвигается: will становится would.
exampleOk: He said he would come later.
exampleBad: He said he will come later.
l1Trap: Время в придаточном оставляют как в прямой речи.

title: reported questions
rule: In a reported question the word order is normal and do or did disappear. Yes or no questions use if or whether.
ruleRu: В косвенном вопросе порядок слов прямой, do и did исчезают. Вопросы да или нет — через if или whether.
exampleOk: He asked if I wanted coffee.
exampleBad: He asked did I want coffee.
l1Trap: Вопросительный порядок оставляют внутри косвенного вопроса.

title: want to
rule: Want, hope, decide, plan and need take to plus the base verb. I want to leave. Not I want leave.
ruleRu: Want, hope, decide, need требуют to и глагол. I want to leave.
exampleOk: They decided to wait.
exampleBad: They decided waiting.
l1Trap: To после want пропускают или ставят -ing.

title: verb plus -ing
rule: Enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep and practise take verb-ing, not to. I enjoy cooking.
ruleRu: Enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep требуют -ing, не to.
exampleOk: She suggested taking a taxi.
exampleBad: She enjoys to cook.
l1Trap: После всех глаголов ставят to, как после want.

title: preposition plus -ing
rule: A verb immediately after a preposition takes -ing. Thank you for helping. I'm interested in learning.
ruleRu: Глагол сразу после предлога стоит в -ing. Thank you for helping.
exampleOk: He left without saying goodbye.
exampleBad: He left without say goodbye.
l1Trap: После предлога ставят начальную форму.

title: stop doing and stop to do
titleRu: Stop doing и stop to do
rule: Stop doing means finish that activity. Stop to do means pause in order to do something else.
ruleRu: Stop doing — бросить это занятие. Stop to do — остановиться, чтобы сделать другое.
exampleOk: He stopped talking when the film started.
exampleBad: He stopped to talk when the film started, so he was quiet.
l1Trap: Обе конструкции переводят «перестал», и смысл меняется.

title: like doing and would like to
titleRu: Like doing и would like to
rule: Like doing is a general taste. Would like to do is a wish now.
ruleRu: Like doing — вообще нравится. Would like to — хочу сейчас или скоро.
exampleOk: I like cooking, and tonight I'd like to cook fish.
exampleBad: I would like cooking tonight.
l1Trap: Would теряют, и конкретное желание звучит как характер.

title: let and make
rule: Let and make are followed by a person and the base verb, with no to. In the passive, make takes to: I was made to wait.
ruleRu: После let и make — человек и глагол без to. В пассиве у make появляется to.
exampleOk: My parents let me stay out.
exampleBad: My parents let me to stay out.
l1Trap: To ставят после let и make, как после allow.

title: comparative
rule: Short adjectives take -er. Long adjectives take more. Do not use both. Than introduces the other thing.
ruleRu: Короткие прилагательные — -er. Длинные — more. Нельзя more better. Вторую часть вводит than.
exampleOk: This bag is cheaper than that one.
exampleBad: This bag is more cheaper then that one.
l1Trap: More и -er ставят вместе, а than пишут как then.

title: than and then
rule: Than is for comparison. Then is for time, the next moment.
ruleRu: Than — сравнение. Then — потом.
exampleOk: I'd rather walk than wait.
exampleBad: I'd rather walk then wait.
l1Trap: Then пишут в сравнениях, потому что слова звучат похоже.

title: as ... as
rule: As plus adjective plus as means equal. The negative is not as tall as. Do not use than here.
ruleRu: As, прилагательное, as — равенство. Отрицание — not as tall as. Than здесь не нужен.
exampleOk: It isn't as cold as yesterday.
exampleBad: It isn't so cold than yesterday.
l1Trap: Конструкцию собирают из so и than.

title: superlative
rule: The superlative needs the. Short adjectives take -est: the oldest. Long ones take the most. Not the most oldest.
ruleRu: Превосходная степень требует the. Короткие — the oldest. Длинные — the most interesting.
exampleOk: It was the best day of the trip.
exampleBad: It was best day of the trip.
l1Trap: The перед превосходной степенью пропускают.

title: too and enough
rule: Too goes before the adjective and means more than is good. Enough goes after the adjective. Too expensive. Old enough.
ruleRu: Too — слишком, перед прилагательным. Enough — достаточно, после прилагательного.
exampleOk: The coffee is too hot. She is old enough to drive.
exampleBad: The coffee is too much hot. She is enough old to drive.
l1Trap: Enough ставят перед прилагательным, а too усиливают через much.

title: so and such
rule: So goes before an adjective alone: so tired. Such goes before a noun phrase: such a long day.
ruleRu: So — перед прилагательным без существительного. Such — перед группой с существительным.
exampleOk: It was such a cold evening that we stayed in.
exampleBad: It was so a cold evening that we stayed in.
l1Trap: So ставят перед a и существительным.

title: in, on, at for time
rule: At a clock time: at 7. On a day: on Monday. In a month, year or part of the day: in June, in the morning.
ruleRu: At — час. On — день и дата. In — месяц, год, время суток: in the morning.
exampleOk: The meeting is on Friday at 10 in the morning.
exampleBad: The meeting is in Friday at the morning.
l1Trap: Один русский предлог «в» закрывает все три случая.

title: in, on, at for place
rule: At a point, on a surface, in a space. At the door. On the table. In the room.
ruleRu: At — точка. On — поверхность. In — объём и город.
exampleOk: She is at the station, in the cafe.
exampleBad: She is in the station door, on the room.
l1Trap: In и at меняют местами.

title: by and until
rule: By is a deadline, at or before that point. Until means the situation continues up to that point.
ruleRu: By — крайний срок, не позже. Until — действие тянется до этого момента.
exampleOk: Please send it by Monday. The shop is open until 8.
exampleBad: Please send it until Monday.
l1Trap: Оба переводят «до», и дедлайн путают с длительностью.

title: depend on
rule: Depend, rely and insist take on, not of or from. It depends on the weather.
ruleRu: Depend, rely, insist требуют on, не of и не from.
exampleOk: It depends on you.
exampleBad: It depends of you.
l1Trap: Of переносят из «зависеть от».

title: arrive in and at
rule: Arrive in a city or country, arrive at a building. Arrive home has no preposition. Not arrive to.
ruleRu: Arrive in — город и страна, arrive at — здание. Arrive home без предлога. Arrive to не говорят.
exampleOk: We arrived in Rome and then at the hotel.
exampleBad: We arrived to Rome and then to the hotel.
l1Trap: To ставят по русскому «приехать в».

title: listen to
rule: Listen needs to before an object. Hear does not take to. Listen to me. I heard a noise.
ruleRu: Перед дополнением у listen нужен to. Hear предлога to не требует.
exampleOk: Listen to this song. I can hear the drums.
exampleBad: Listen this song. I can hear to the drums.
l1Trap: To после listen забывают, а после hear добавляют.

title: good at, interested in
rule: Good at, interested in, afraid of, famous for, married to. The preposition is fixed.
ruleRu: Предлог после прилагательного фиксирован: good at, interested in, afraid of, married to.
exampleOk: She is good at maths and interested in history.
exampleBad: She is good in maths and interested at history.
l1Trap: In и at меняют, потому что по-русски «хорош в».

title: wait for
rule: Wait needs for before a noun. Look forward to is followed by verb-ing: I look forward to meeting you.
ruleRu: Wait требует for. Look forward to — и после to глагол с -ing.
exampleOk: I'll wait for you. I look forward to seeing you.
exampleBad: I'll wait you. I look forward to see you.
l1Trap: For после wait нет, а после look forward to ставят начальную форму.

title: home without a preposition
rule: Go home, come home and arrive home have no to. At home is for location. Home is where you live; a house is the building.
ruleRu: Go home и arrive home — без to. At home — когда вы уже там. House — здание.
exampleOk: I went home at six.
exampleBad: I went to home at six.
l1Trap: Говорят go to home и go at home.

title: question word order
rule: In most questions an auxiliary comes before the subject. Where do you live? Not Where you live?
ruleRu: В обычном вопросе вспомогательный глагол стоит перед подлежащим. Where do you live?
exampleOk: Why did they leave?
exampleBad: Why they left?
l1Trap: Вопрос делают только интонацией, без do или did.

title: subject questions
rule: When who or what is the subject, do not add do or did. Who called you? Who did you call? is a different question.
ruleRu: Если who или what — подлежащее, do и did не нужны. Who called you?
exampleOk: Who broke the cup?
exampleBad: Who did break the cup?
l1Trap: Did вставляют в любой вопрос с who.

title: indirect questions
rule: After Could you tell me and Do you know, use statement order. Could you tell me where the station is?
ruleRu: После Could you tell me порядок слов прямой. Could you tell me where the station is?
exampleOk: Do you know what time it is?
exampleBad: Do you know what time is it?
l1Trap: Внутри вежливой рамки оставляют обычный вопрос.

title: negatives with do
rule: Ordinary verbs need don't, doesn't or didn't. Not alone is not enough. I don't know.
ruleRu: Обычному глаголу нужно don't, doesn't или didn't. Одного not мало.
exampleOk: I didn't understand the last part.
exampleBad: I not understood the last part.
l1Trap: Not ставят перед глаголом, как русское «не», без do.

title: adjective before the noun
rule: An adjective goes before the noun and does not become plural. A red car. Two red cars.
ruleRu: Прилагательное стоит перед существительным и не получает -s во множественном.
exampleOk: They live in a small flat.
exampleBad: They live in a flat small.
l1Trap: Прилагательное ставят после существительного и иногда с -s.

title: because and so
rule: Because introduces the reason. So introduces the result. Do not use both in the same link.
ruleRu: Because — причина, so — следствие. В одной связи нужно что-то одно.
exampleOk: She was ill, so she stayed at home.
exampleBad: Because she was ill, so she stayed at home.
l1Trap: Because и so ставят вместе, как «потому что, поэтому».

title: although and but
rule: Although and but both show contrast, but not together. Although it was late, we stayed. Or: It was late, but we stayed.
ruleRu: Although и but оба про противопоставление, но вместе их не ставят.
exampleOk: Although he was tired, he finished the work.
exampleBad: Although he was tired, but he finished the work.
l1Trap: Как русское «хотя, но», but оставляют после although.

title: despite
rule: Despite and in spite of take a noun or verb-ing. Despite of is wrong. Despite the rain. In spite of the rain.
ruleRu: Despite и in spite of требуют существительное или -ing. Despite of не говорят.
exampleOk: Despite the noise, I slept.
exampleBad: Despite of the noise, I slept.
l1Trap: Of добавляют к despite по аналогии с in spite of.

title: who and which
rule: Who is for people. Which is for things. That can replace either in a defining clause.
ruleRu: Who — люди, which — вещи. That может заменить оба в определительном придаточном.
exampleOk: The man who lives upstairs is a pianist.
exampleBad: The man which lives upstairs is a pianist.
l1Trap: Which ставят и к людям, потому что одно русское «который».

title: whose in a clause
rule: Whose shows possession. The student whose phone rang. Not the student who his phone rang.
ruleRu: Whose показывает принадлежность. Не who his phone.
exampleOk: I met a woman whose son is in my class.
exampleBad: I met a woman who her son is in my class.
l1Trap: Вместо whose строят who his.

title: so do I and neither do I
titleRu: So do I и neither do I
rule: Agree with a positive using so plus auxiliary: So do I. Agree with a negative using neither: Neither can I.
ruleRu: Согласиться с плюсом: So do I. Согласиться с минусом: Neither do I.
exampleOk: I can't swim. Neither can I.
exampleBad: I can't swim. So can't I.
l1Trap: На отрицание отвечают so don't I.

title: question tags
rule: A positive sentence takes a negative tag, and the auxiliary is repeated. You live here, don't you? Not isn't it for every sentence.
ruleRu: После плюса — минус, после минуса — плюс. В хвосте тот же вспомогательный глагол. Не isn't it на всё подряд.
exampleOk: They have left, haven't they?
exampleBad: They have left, isn't it?
l1Trap: На любой хвост ставят isn't it, как одно «не так ли».

title: one negative is enough
rule: English does not stack negatives. I didn't see anyone. Not I didn't see nobody.
ruleRu: В английском одно отрицание. I didn't see anyone. Не didn't see nobody.
exampleOk: I didn't tell anybody.
exampleBad: I didn't tell nobody.
l1Trap: Двойное отрицание из русского «никому не сказал» переносят целиком.

title: do and make
rule: Do is for tasks: do homework, do business. Make is for a result: make a mistake, make a decision, make a cake.
ruleRu: Do — работа и занятие. Make — создать результат: mistake, decision, cake.
exampleOk: I made a mistake while I was doing my homework.
exampleBad: I did a mistake while I was making my homework.
l1Trap: Оба значат «делать», и mistake с homework получают не тот глагол.

title: speak and talk
rule: Speak is for a language: speak English. Talk is a conversation: talk to a friend. Tell needs a person and information.
ruleRu: Speak — язык. Talk — разговор. Tell — сказать кому-то информацию.
exampleOk: She speaks three languages and talked to me for an hour.
exampleBad: She talks three languages.
l1Trap: Speak, talk, say и tell все становятся «говорить» без разбора.

title: lend and borrow
rule: Lend is give for a time. Borrow is take for a time. Can you lend me a pen? Can I borrow your pen?
ruleRu: Lend — дать на время. Borrow — взять на время.
exampleOk: She lent me her umbrella.
exampleBad: She borrowed me her umbrella.
l1Trap: Одно русское «одолжить» покрывает обе стороны.

title: bring and take
rule: Bring is towards the speaker. Take is away. Bring the book here. Take this home.
ruleRu: Bring — к говорящему. Take — оттуда.
exampleOk: Can you bring your passport when you come?
exampleBad: Can you take your passport when you come here?
l1Trap: Оба переводят «принести» без направления.

title: see, look, watch
rule: See is notice. Look needs at and is on purpose. Watch is follow something that moves: a film, a match.
ruleRu: See — увидеть. Look at — смотреть намеренно. Watch — следить за тем, что меняется.
exampleOk: Look at that bird. We watched the match.
exampleBad: Look that bird.
l1Trap: Все три — «смотреть», и at после look пропадает.

title: job and work
rule: Job is countable: a job. Work meaning employment is uncountable: a lot of work, not a work.
ruleRu: Job считается: a job. Work в значении «работа» не считается: much work, не a work.
exampleOk: She is looking for a job because she needs work.
exampleBad: She is looking for a work.
l1Trap: Work получают артикль a, как русское «работа».

title: another and other
rule: Another is one more, singular. Other is the remaining ones. Not an other.
ruleRu: Another — ещё один. Other — остальные. Не an other.
exampleOk: Would you like another biscuit?
exampleBad: Would you like an other biscuit?
l1Trap: Another разбирают на an other или ставят с множественным.

title: also, too, either
rule: Also and too add to a positive sentence. Either is for negatives. I don't like it either. Not I don't like it too.
ruleRu: Also и too — в утверждениях. В отрицании — either, не too.
exampleOk: My brother doesn't like it either.
exampleBad: My brother doesn't like it too.
l1Trap: Too ставят и в отрицание, как русское «тоже».

title: each and every
rule: Each and every take a singular noun and a singular verb. Every student has a book.
ruleRu: Each и every требуют единственное число. Every student has.
exampleOk: Each of them knows the answer.
exampleBad: Each of them know the answer.
l1Trap: После each of ставят глагол во множественном.

title: both, either, neither
rule: Both takes a plural verb. Either and neither take a singular verb. Neither of them is ready.
ruleRu: Both — глагол во множественном. Either и neither — в единственном.
exampleOk: Neither answer is correct.
exampleBad: Neither answers are correct.
l1Trap: Neither получает множественное, как русское «оба не».

title: actual is not topical
rule: Actual means real, not imagined. Current or topical is the word for something important now.
ruleRu: Actual значит «фактический», не «актуальный». Для «актуальный» — current или topical.
exampleOk: The actual price is on the label.
exampleBad: This is a very actual topic.
l1Trap: Actual читают как «актуальный».

title: accurate and tidy
rule: Accurate means correct and exact. Tidy or neat means orderly.
ruleRu: Accurate — точный. «Аккуратный» про порядок — neat или tidy.
exampleOk: Her measurements were accurate, and her desk was tidy.
exampleBad: Her room is very accurate.
l1Trap: Accurate используют про опрятную комнату.

title: magazine is a periodical
rule: A magazine is something you read. A shop or a store is where you buy things.
ruleRu: Magazine — журнал. Магазин — a shop или a store.
exampleOk: I bought the magazine in a shop.
exampleBad: I bought shoes in a magazine.
l1Trap: Magazine читают как «магазин».

title: fabric and factory
rule: Fabric is cloth. A factory is a place where things are made.
ruleRu: Fabric — ткань. Factory — завод.
exampleOk: The factory produces cotton fabric.
exampleBad: He works at a big fabric outside the city.
l1Trap: Fabric используют как «фабрика».

title: chef and chief
rule: A chef is a professional cook. A chief is the person in charge.
ruleRu: Chef — шеф-повар. Chief — руководитель.
exampleOk: The chef trained for years.
exampleBad: The chef of our department signed the letter.
l1Trap: Chef читают как «шеф» в смысле начальник.

title: sympathetic
rule: Sympathetic means kind to someone in trouble. Likeable or pleasant is the word for a person you simply enjoy.
ruleRu: Sympathetic — тот, кто сочувствует. «Симпатичный» — likeable, nice, pleasant.
exampleOk: The doctor was sympathetic about the pain.
exampleBad: He is a sympathetic young man everyone wants to date.
l1Trap: Sympathetic используют как «симпатичный».

title: be used to
rule: Be used to plus a noun or verb-ing means it is familiar. This is not used to for a past habit.
ruleRu: Be used to и существительное или -ing — «мне это привычно». Это не used to про прошлое.
exampleOk: I am used to the noise now.
exampleBad: I am used to get up early now.
l1Trap: После be used to ставят инфинитив.

title: get used to
rule: Get used to is the process of becoming familiar. Be used to is the state after that. The verb after to is -ing.
ruleRu: Get used to — процесс привыкания. После to глагол с -ing.
exampleOk: I got used to the hours.
exampleBad: I got used to work nights.
l1Trap: После get used to забывают -ing.

title: had better
rule: Had better plus the base verb is strong advice for now. There is no to, and it stays had. Not have better.
ruleRu: Had better и глагол без to — настойчивый совет. Had не меняется на have.
exampleOk: We had better hurry.
exampleBad: We have better to hurry.
l1Trap: Had меняют на have и добавляют to.

title: would rather
rule: Would rather plus the base verb means prefer. No to. I'd rather walk than drive.
ruleRu: Would rather и глагол без to — «предпочёл бы».
exampleOk: I'd rather not talk about it.
exampleBad: I'd rather to not talk about it.
l1Trap: После rather ставят to.

title: supposed to
rule: Be supposed to means the rule or other people expect this. It does not mean I think. The form is supposed, with -d.
ruleRu: Be supposed to — так положено. Не «я полагаю». Форма supposed, с -d.
exampleOk: You're not supposed to park here.
exampleBad: You don't suppose to park here.
l1Trap: Suppose понимают как «предполагать» и теряют be и -d.

title: it's time
rule: It's time to go is neutral. It's time plus a subject takes the past simple when you mean it should already be happening: It's time we left.
ruleRu: It's time to go — просто пора. It's time we left — пора бы уже, глагол в past simple.
exampleOk: It's time we left.
exampleBad: It's time we leave.
l1Trap: После it's time и подлежащего оставляют настоящее время.

title: have something done
rule: Have plus object plus past participle means someone else does it for you. I had my hair cut.
ruleRu: Have, дополнение и третья форма — тебе это сделали. I had my hair cut.
exampleOk: We had the roof repaired.
exampleBad: We had repaired the roof by a builder.
l1Trap: Конструкцию путают с past perfect.

title: hardly
rule: Hardly means almost not. Do not add another not. Hard means with effort: work hard. Hardly ever means almost never.
ruleRu: Hardly — «почти не», второе отрицание не нужно. Hard — «усердно».
exampleOk: I could hardly hear him.
exampleBad: I couldn't hardly hear him.
l1Trap: Hardly усиливают через not и путают с hard.

title: negative inversion
rule: When Never or Not only starts the sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject. Never have I seen that.
ruleRu: Если фразу начинает Never или Not only, вспомогательный глагол встаёт перед подлежащим.
exampleOk: Rarely do we get such weather.
exampleBad: Rarely we get such weather.
l1Trap: Порядок слов оставляют прямым.

title: mixed conditional
rule: A past cause with a present result: if plus past perfect, and would plus the base verb for now.
ruleRu: Причина в прошлом, результат сейчас: if и past perfect, дальше would и глагол про настоящее.
exampleOk: If she had taken the job, she would live in Berlin now.
exampleBad: If she had taken the job, she would have lived in Berlin now.
l1Trap: Обе части ставят в третьем типе, и «сейчас» пропадает.

title: hundred without -s
rule: After a number, hundred, thousand and million stay singular. Two hundred. Hundreds of is only for a vague number.
ruleRu: После числа hundred, thousand, million без -s. Hundreds of — только когда число туманное.
exampleOk: There were three hundred people.
exampleBad: There were three hundreds people.
l1Trap: S добавляют даже после точного числа.

title: it takes
rule: It takes plus time plus to plus verb says how long an activity needs. It takes me twenty minutes to get there.
ruleRu: It takes, время и to с глаголом — сколько времени нужно.
exampleOk: It took us an hour to fix it.
exampleBad: We took an hour for fix it.
l1Trap: Подлежащим делают человека, и for ставят вместо to.
